name: Ragi Dosa
description: A healthy South Indian breakfast option made with finger millet (ragi) flour, rich in calcium and iron.
ingredients: 1 cup ragi flour, 1/2 cup rice flour, 1/4 cup urad dal flour, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 green chili (finely chopped), 1 small onion (finely chopped), 1/4 cup chopped coriander leaves, Salt to taste, Water as needed
instructions: 1. Mix all the flours together in a bowl. 2. Add cumin seeds, green chili, onion, coriander leaves, and salt. 3. Add water gradually to make a batter of pouring consistency. 4. Heat a non-stick pan, pour a ladle of batter and spread it in a circular motion. 5. Cook on medium heat until the edges become crisp. 6. Flip and cook the other side for a minute. 7. Serve hot with coconut chutney or sambar.

name: Palak Paneer
description: A classic North Indian dish made with spinach and cottage cheese, packed with protein and iron.
ingredients: 250g paneer (cottage cheese), 2 bunches spinach, 2 tomatoes, 1 onion, 2 green chilies, 1 inch ginger, 4 cloves garlic, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1/2 tsp turmeric powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala, 2 tbsp oil, Salt to taste
instructions: 1. Blanch spinach in hot water, drain, and blend into a puree. 2. Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds. 3. Add chopped onions, ginger, garlic, and green chilies. 4. Once golden, add tomatoes and cook until soft. 5. Add turmeric, coriander powder, and salt. 6. Add spinach puree and simmer for 5 minutes. 7. Add paneer cubes and garam masala. 8. Cook for another 5 minutes. 9. Serve hot with roti or rice.

name: Masala Chai
description: A soothing Indian spiced tea that aids digestion and boosts immunity.
ingredients: 1 cup water, 1/2 cup milk, 1 tsp tea leaves, 2-3 cardamom pods, 1 small cinnamon stick, 2-3 cloves, 1 small piece ginger, 1-2 tsp sugar (optional)
instructions: 1. Crush the spices slightly. 2. Boil water in a saucepan. 3. Add crushed spices and ginger. 4. Add tea leaves and simmer for a minute. 5. Add milk and bring to a boil. 6. Add sugar if using. 7. Strain and serve hot.

name: Sprouts Chaat
description: A nutritious and tangy snack made with sprouted mung beans and chickpeas.
ingredients: 1 cup mixed sprouts (mung beans, chickpeas), 1 small onion (finely chopped), 1 small tomato (chopped), 1 small cucumber (chopped), 1 green chili (finely chopped), 1/4 cup chopped coriander leaves, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1/2 tsp chaat masala, 1/4 tsp cumin powder, Salt to taste
instructions: 1. In a bowl, combine all the sprouts. 2. Add onion, tomato, cucumber, and green chili. 3. Add coriander leaves, lemon juice, chaat masala, cumin powder, and salt. 4. Toss well to combine. 5. Serve immediately as a healthy snack.

name: Dal Tadka
description: A protein-rich lentil dish with aromatic tempering, perfect for daily consumption.
ingredients: 1 cup yellow moong dal, 1/2 tsp turmeric powder, 1 tsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 2 dried red chilies, 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 small onion (finely chopped), 1 small tomato (chopped), 1/2 tsp coriander powder, 1/4 tsp garam masala, Fresh coriander leaves for garnish, Salt to taste
instructions: 1. Wash and soak dal for 30 minutes. 2. Pressure cook with turmeric and salt until soft. 3. Heat ghee in a pan, add cumin and mustard seeds. 4. Once they splutter, add dried red chilies and ginger-garlic paste. 5. Add onions and sauté until golden. 6. Add tomatoes, coriander powder and cook until soft. 7. Add cooked dal and simmer for 5 minutes. 8. Add garam masala and garnish with fresh coriander. 9. Serve hot with rice or roti.

name: Oats Idli
description: A healthy twist to traditional South Indian idli, made with oats for added fiber.
ingredients: 1 cup oats, 1/2 cup semolina (sooji), 1/2 cup yogurt, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp urad dal, 1 tsp chana dal, 1 green chili (finely chopped), 1 tsp ginger (grated), Few curry leaves, 1 tbsp oil, Salt to taste
instructions: 1. Dry roast oats and grind to a coarse powder. 2. In a bowl, mix ground oats, semolina, yogurt, and salt. 3. Add water to make a thick batter. Let it rest for 15 minutes. 4. Heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds, urad dal, and chana dal. 5. Once they splutter, add green chili, ginger, and curry leaves. 6. Add this tempering to the batter. 7. Add baking soda and mix well. 8. Pour the batter into greased idli molds. 9. Steam for 10-12 minutes. 10. Serve hot with coconut chutney.

name: Vegetable Khichdi
description: A complete one-pot meal with rice, lentils, and mixed vegetables, ideal for easy digestion.
ingredients: 1/2 cup rice, 1/2 cup moong dal, 1 cup mixed vegetables (carrots, peas, beans), 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1/2 tsp turmeric powder, 1 tsp ghee, 1 small onion (chopped), 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 small tomato (chopped), 1/2 tsp garam masala, Fresh coriander leaves for garnish, Salt to taste
instructions: 1. Wash and soak rice and dal for 30 minutes. 2. Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, add cumin seeds. 3. Add onions and sauté until golden. 4. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for a minute. 5. Add mixed vegetables and tomatoes. 6. Add turmeric, salt, and drained rice and dal. 7. Add 3 cups of water and pressure cook for 3 whistles. 8. Once pressure releases, add garam masala and garnish with coriander leaves. 9. Serve hot with yogurt or pickle.

name: Beet and Carrot Raita
description: A cooling yogurt-based side dish packed with the goodness of beetroot and carrots.
ingredients: 1 cup yogurt, 1/2 cup grated beetroot, 1/2 cup grated carrot, 1/2 tsp cumin powder, 1/4 tsp black salt, 1/4 tsp regular salt, 1 tsp chopped mint leaves, 1 tsp chopped coriander leaves
instructions: 1. Whisk yogurt until smooth. 2. Add grated beetroot and carrot. 3. Add cumin powder, black salt, and regular salt. 4. Mix well and garnish with mint and coriander leaves. 5. Serve chilled as a side dish with biryani or pulao.
